prompt: A single wide illustration of an open-plan office, arranged along one diagonal path. In the lower-left corner, for contrast, a small chatbot terminal is tethered to a desk, exchanging one speech bubble with a user and then dimming to wait for the next message; everything else in the frame belongs to the agent. The agent is a slender robot whose transparent head holds a glowing swirl of printed words — the language model at its core — and it strides along a trail of stepping stones that it lays down just ahead of its own feet, numbering each step itself as it carries a slip stamped GOAL toward a distant flag reading GOAL MET. The stones are labeled with its real-world actions — browsing the web, sending messages, filling in forms, spending money, hiring a small figure who signs a contract — while the stones already crossed show what is at stake: one cracked, one spilling coins from a struck purse, one littered with crumpled paperwork, its mistakes leaving real dents in the world. Its judgement visibly consists only of what it carries: a satchel stenciled MEMORY bulging with notes and a rulebook titled INSTRUCTIONS buckled at its waist. Humans crowd the edges of the frame: eager managers in suits watch from cubicles clutching ledgers, while one supervisor walks at the robot's shoulder, prompting it through a megaphone, bolting a guardrail of checkpoint gates around its path, and snatching a red bug-shaped ERROR out of the air before it lands; a background sign reads AGENT-RUN BUSINESS, TRIAL 7, and beneath it the supervisor's clipboard tallies a long list of previous catches.
